findings.text: Exposes a query operation that maps a VMX capability MSR index to a 64-bit value derived from cached nested state, reporting success for recognized indices and a distinct failure status for unknown ones.

Paired TRUE and legacy control reports share the same stored low and high halves combined into one value, while the legacy variant additionally forces a small set of always-on bits; miscellaneous and second-level controls use the same combining rule without extra bits.

The nested capability cache observed through the query holds separate entries for basic info, pin, processor, exit and entry control halves, misc halves, fixed CR bounds, enumeration, secondary halves, EPT plus VPID capabilities and VMFUNC controls.

The interface speaks the architectural IA32 VMX capability MSR family for basic, pin, processor, exit, entry, misc, fixed CR, enumeration, secondary, EPT/VPID and VMFUNC reports, with EPT occupying the low half and VPID the high half of one entry.

Guest/host MSR sampling guards the hardware access with a preemption-off section and only refreshes the cached copy when guest state is currently loaded, otherwise returning the last cached value unchanged.
Provides a reader for the guest kernel GS base that delegates to the generic guest/host MSR sampler with a dedicated per-CPU cache slot.
Top-level intercept refresh bypasses all reprogramming for trust-domain vCPUs, where MSR filtering happens during emulated calls, and otherwise refreshes both instruction and MSR interception state.

MSR interception refresh is a no-op without bitmap support in hardware; when supported it unconditionally allows direct guest access to time, segment bases and system-call entry registers, plus power and frequency counters only when the owning VM has disabled those exits.

Remaining MSR interception is feature-gated: tracing controls follow host-guest tracing mode, extended-feature, speculation, prediction, flush, shadow-stack and branch-tracking MSRs are intercepted exactly when the guest lacks the corresponding capability or host enablement says otherwise, and performance MSRs defer to a dedicated helper.

Mediated-PMU refresh is inert unless that mode is enabled globally; otherwise it toggles load/save of the global performance control around entries and exits, uses an autostore fallback on older hardware, passes virtualized counters through while forcing interception of unowned counters, and intercepts global status and overflow controls according to need.

Reported performance capabilities read as zero unless the guest sees the relevant capability leaf, otherwise they come from per-vCPU state; firmware-write permission for counter MSRs is determined by one bit inside that value.
Instruction interception refresh only adjusts whether the performance-counter read instruction causes an exit, following a higher-level need predicate.
Completion of an emulated MSR operation dispatches by vCPU kind to a trust-domain path or the conventional VMX path.

Trust-domain completion reports an invalid-operand status to the caller on error and, on successful reads, publishes the combined data registers as the call result; the compiled-in variant always signals completion while a header fallback signals no action.
System-management-interrupt admission treats trust-domain vCPUs as a bug, reports busy when a nested run is already pending, and otherwise allows entry only outside system-management mode.

Entering system-management mode records whether the vCPU was in guest context and whether nested virtualization was active, exits to host context if needed, deactivates nesting and clears halt state; leaving restores nesting activation and, when returning to guest context, validates saved state and schedules re-entry, signalling fault on invalid state.
Halt-state clearing only writes the activity field when halt is permitted inside the guest and the current activity indicates halt, moving it to active without adjusting the instruction pointer.

Nested entry saves host debugging, bound, CET and paging context, switches to the L2 control structure, merges early controls, validates guest state and entry controls, loads entry MSRs or defers page acquisition outside entry, re-evaluates pending events when windows or interrupts may have opened, then arms the preemption timer and reports success while leaving the return to L1 pending until L2 exits.

Failed nested entry unwinds time offset and translation flushes, leaves guest mode, switches back to the L1 control structure, releases acquired pages and loads host state on the entry path, records an invalid-state or MSR-load failure reason with detail, and marks shadow synchronization when shadowing is active.

Emulated preemption timing derives from L1 time scaled by a fixed shift, caches a deadline on first use and returns the remainder; a zero remainder expires synchronously, zero virtual frequency disables arming, otherwise the value is scaled to nanoseconds and armed as an absolute pinned timer whose expiry flags expiration, requests event processing and kicks the vCPU.

Early L2 control preparation starts from host desires, merges L1 pin, basic and secondary requests with masking, takes posted-interrupt and several virtualization features only from L1, forces unconditional port exits without bitmaps, preserves prior MSR-bitmap use, disables emulated logging and shadowing, and presets descriptor exiting when emulating user-mode protection with that guest bit set.
